bone.$description: Bone — Page canvas, primary card surface — the off-white paper tone the entire interface sits on, warm enough to feel linen, not bright enough to feel clinical

ink.$description: Ink — All body type, primary action border, all interactive strokes — the only dark in the system, pure black rather than warm charcoal to create maximum contrast against the cream canvas

stone.$description: Stone — Card borders, hairline dividers, subtle section breaks — the warm gray-beige that separates elements without drawing attention

linen.$description: Linen — Hairline borders, dividers, input outlines, and card edges on light surfaces. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

graphite.$description: Graphite — Card secondary text, muted metadata, price-adjacent labels — the mid-gray that recedes behind the primary ink-black headlines

silt.$description: Silt — Neutral form states, badge text, and quiet UI feedback where color should stay understated. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

blush.$description: Blush — Decorative accent surface, soft wash behind editorial text blocks, occasional section tints — the dusty rose that nods to botanical petals without becoming saccharine

citron.$description: Citron — Promotional highlight surface — used sparingly as a wash behind sale tags, value bundle badges, or limited-edition callouts; pale enough to never compete with product photography

pp-right-grotesk.$description: Display headlines and section titles — weight 200 is anti-convention for commerce; the ultra-thin strokes create a calligraphic, editorial whisper that treats product names as poetry rather than slogans. Tight tracking (-0.015em) pulls the delicate strokes into a cohesive block.

shne.$description: Primary body, UI, navigation, product names, buttons — the workhorse neutral grotesque. Weight 400 for body copy keeps a quiet editorial feel; weight 500 for navigation and product names adds enough presence to guide the eye. Slight positive tracking on uppercase labels opens them up to read as proper editorial tags.

shne-mono.$description: Micro-labels and scent-family tags — used for 'SMOKY & MEDITATIVE', 'BUTTERY & SOFT', 'VALUE BUNDLE' type annotations. The monospace width and widened tracking (0.05em) give these labels a scientific, museum-catalog quality that contrasts with the organic display type.
